Democratic Party merger negotiations underway as political leadership struggle intensifies
Analysis of President Lee Jae-myung's judicial risks and realignment of opposition dynamics
editorials.bodyTr:
Former lawmaker Cho Kuk has expressed a negative stance on canceling the prosecution of President Lee Jae-myung, signaling a power struggle for political leadership ahead of merger negotiations with the Democratic Party. This editorial examines the president's judicial risks and shifting dynamics within the opposition camp.

The president faces mounting legal pressure as multiple cases continue through the courts. The question of whether to pursue or suspend prosecution has become a critical issue dividing the opposition coalition. Cho's position carries particular weight given his influence within certain political circles and his potential role in any party realignment.

The timing of these statements is significant. As talks progress between different opposition factions seeking to strengthen their collective position, questions about party leadership and direction have intensified. Those advocating for dropping the charges argue it would ease political tension and allow the president to focus on governance. Critics counter that such a move would appear as political favoritism and undermine judicial independence.

The broader implications extend beyond the immediate legal question. How the opposition handles this issue will shape perceptions of its commitment to rule of law and fair process. It also reflects internal struggles over who will chart the party's future course and what principles will guide its actions.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Kim Seung-won's Text Message Favor-Seeking and Prosecution Deferral Must Be Thoroughly Investigated
summaryTr: Kim Seung-won, the nominee for Justice Minister, has been given a suspended prosecution for soliciting approval of a clinical trial from the Food and Drug Administration.
Two weeks after the solicitation, Genencel's clinical trial was approved, and the largest shareholder sold their stake for 6.3 billion won.
It must be thoroughly investigated whether the approval of a clinical trial—which concerns public health—was exploited to inflate corporate value.
editorial.bodyTr: It has come to light that Kim Seung-won, the nominee for justice minister, was investigated by prosecutors and received a deferred prosecution decision in connection with a past case involving alleged solicitation for clinical trial approval at the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. However, the circumstances surrounding the matter are murky. Given that the justice minister oversees prosecutorial personnel and legal administration, it is necessary to thoroughly investigate the related suspicions. In October 2021, when he was a first-term lawmaker, nominee Kim received a request from an acquaintance surnamed Yang and sent a text message to Kim Gang-lip, then head of the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, asking him to expedite the processing of a clinical trial for a COVID-19 treatment candidate submitted by biotech company Genencell. After receiving a reply from Director Kim stating that he would pass the matter along to his staff, nominee Kim forwarded this to Yang. Two weeks later, on October 26, the ministry approved Genencell's clinical trial plan. It was also revealed that Kang, a major shareholder of Genencell at the time, attempted to send 5 million won in campaign contributions to nominee Kim's side. Between nominee Kim's text solicitation and the ministry's approval, on October 19, 2021, Kang sold 14 percent of Genencell shares to a Kosdaq-listed company for 6.3 billion won and separately received investment in convertible bonds worth 5 billion won. The Kosdaq company that became Genencell's largest shareholder subsequently actively promoted the candidate substance in question. Prosecutors investigated the case and indicted Yang and Kang on charges including bribery, but granted nominee Kim deferred prosecution in December 2024. Deferred prosecution is a measure in which criminal suspicions are acknowledged but the case is not sent to trial in light of various circumstances. Nominee Kim filed a constitutional complaint, claiming the decision was unjust. While nominee Kim claims he merely relayed a civil petition, it is difficult to view his actions as responsible conduct for a member of parliament. According to the first-trial judgment against Kang, it appears Genencell submitted materials with false experimental results and deleted information about side effects to obtain approval from the ministry. Subsequently, the clinical trial was not properly conducted. How can an issue of clinical trial approval, which directly affects public health and safety, be handled in this manner? It is questionable whether the ministry's approval ultimately became material used for Genencell's share sale and enhancing the corporate value of the Kosdaq-listed company. Therefore, a parliamentary hearing must also scrutinize whether the ministry properly handled its duties at the time and whether the prosecution's deferred prosecution decision was appropriate. If necessary, additional investigations and inquiries should follow.

editorial.title: Budget built on boom
editorial.body: Government spending is surging on the back of chip-driven tax windfall that may not last The government’s budget proposal for next year, totaling 820.9 trillion won ($599 billion), is the largest ever. The 12.8 percent year-on-year rise and the 92 trillion won increase are also the largest on record. The government’s ability to ramp up spending so substantially is due above all to an exceptional tax revenue windfall brought about by the semiconductor supercycle. The ambitious 162 trillion won Future Response Fund, too, would not have been possible without the surge in corporate tax revenues caused by the semiconductor boom. One cannot help but question how sustainable such a “superexpansionary budget” is. With national debt almost certain to top 1,500 trillion won next year, the government is jacking up spending at an excessive pace. The government budget surpassed 600 trillion won in 2022 and entered the 700 trillion won range this year, four years later. Next year, however, the figure will cross into the 800 trillion won span after just one year. According to government projections, total spending will continue to rise, surpassing 1,000 trillion won in 2030, the final year of President Lee Jae Myung’s term. Many of the programs funded through the Future Response Fund, including support for local areas and young people, as well as education and childcare for infants and young children, are likely to become ongoing programs rather than one-off expenditures. The government has already pledged to expand welfare programs, including providing 1.2 million won a year from birth through age 18 to help young people become self-reliant and offering free education at national universities in the provinces. If tax revenues decline as the semiconductor industry slows, it is questionable whether whichever administration is in power then will be able to cut such spending. If the government inflates the budget on the assumption that a temporary boom will last, it could fall into a vicious cycle of increasing national debt to make up for declining tax revenues. Temporary revenue gains should not be used to justify permanent spending commitments. Thanks to the surge in tax revenues, the government projects that both the managed fiscal deficit and the national debt-to-GDP ratio will decline next year. This amounts to saying that the government can improve its fiscal health even as it spends more money than ever before. Fiscal health should be judged not by how much the government can spend during a boom, but by whether it can afford to sustain that spending after the boom ends. There are also considerable concerns about chronic wasteful spending in the face of this year’s supersized budget. When the budget is increased sharply all at once, it is only natural that each government ministry will be more tempted to expand existing programs or add new ones. Programs with unclear or overlapping effects, cash handout programs and projects driven by constituency demands are perennial targets of scrutiny. There are also growing concerns that lawmakers’ “note budgets” — pork-barrel projects for their constituencies slipped into the budget at the final stage of deliberations — will become even more rampant ahead of the 2028 general election. The Future Response Fund is no exception. It must not degenerate into a giant government slush fund for catering to politicians’ discretionary demands simply by carrying the name “future.” Sunset provisions should be applied to new programs, while existing programs should be subject to performance evaluations to determine whether they should be continued or discontinued. If the government spends this year’s sharp increase in corporate tax revenues on cash handouts and locks in the resulting spending in ways that make it difficult to cut, it could face serious trouble when the semiconductor industry takes a downturn. The National Assembly must rigorously assess the sustainability of spending and carefully scrutinize the merits of each program to prevent a massive waste of the megasized budget. How S. editorial.bodyTr: 정부 지출이 반도체 슈퍼사이클로 인한 세수 증가에 힘입어 급증하고 있지만, 이러한 호황이 지속될 가능성은 불투명하다. 내년도 예산안 규모는 820조9000억 원으로 역대 최대다. 전년 대비 12.8%의 증가율과 92조 원의 증액 규모도 모두 사상 최고 기록이다. 정부가 이토록 대폭적인 지출 확대를 감행할 수 있는 것은 무엇보다 반도체 슈퍼사이클로 인한 異例的인 세수 증가 때문이다. 야심 찬 162조 원 규모의 미래대응기금 역시 반도체 호황으로 인한 법인세 수입 급증이 없었다면 불가능했을 것이다. 이러한 '초(超)확장적 예산'의 지속가능성에 대해 의문을 제기하지 않을 수 없다. 국가채무가 내년 1500조 원을 넘을 것으로 거의 확실시되는 가운데, 정부는 과도한 속도로 지출을 늘리고 있다. 정부 예산은 2022년 600조 원을 넘긴 후 4년이 지난 올해 700조 원대에 진입했다. 그런데 내년에는 단 1년 만에 800조 원대를 돌파할 것으로 보인다. 정부 전망에 따르면 총 지출은 계속 증가하여 이준석 대통령 임기 마지막 해인 2030년에는 1000조 원을 넘을 것으로 예상된다. 미래대응기금으로 지원되는 지역·청년 지원, 유아 교육·돌봄 등 많은 사업이 일회성 지출이 아닌 항구적 사업으로 정착될 가능성이 높다. 정부는 이미 청년이 18세까지 연 1200만 원을 지급하는 청년자립금 확대와 지방 국립대의 무상교육 제공 등 복지 프로그램 확대를 약속했다. 반도체 산업이 둔화하면서 세수가 감소한다면, 그 때 집권하는 어느 정부라도 이러한 지출을 줄이기 어려울 것이 자명하다. 정부가 일시적 호황이 지속될 것이라는 가정 아래 예산을 부풀린다면, 세수 감소를 메우기 위해 국채를 계속 증발시켜야 하는 악순환에 빠질 수 있다. 일시적 세수 증가가 항구적 지출 약속을 정당화하는 데 쓰여서는 안 된다. 세수 증가에 힘입어 정부는 내년 관리재정수지와 국가채무의 국내총생산(GDP) 대비 비율이 모두 하락할 것으로 전망하고 있다. 이는 정부가 사상 최대의 지출을 하면서도 재정 건전성을 개선할 수 있다는 주장이다. 재정 건전성은 호황 시에 정부가 얼마나 많은 돈을 쓸 수 있는가가 아니라, 호황이 끝난 후에도 그 지출을 감당할 수 있는가로 판단해야 한다. 이번 초(超)규모 예산을 놓고 만성적 낭비 지출에 대한 우려도 상당하다. 예산이 한꺼번에 대폭 증가하면 각 정부 부처가 기존 사업을 확대하거나 새로운 사업을 추가하려는 유혹에 쉽게 빠지는 것은 당연하다. 효과가 불명확하거나 중복되는 사업, 현금 살포 성격의 사업, 지역 이기주의에 따른 사업 등이 항상 점검의 대상이 되어 왔다. 2028년 총선을 앞두고 '의원 예산' 즉 예산 심의 막판에 몰래 집어넣는 지역구 관련 사업이 더욱 판을 치지 않을까 하는 우려도 커지고 있다. 미래대응기금도 예외가 아니다. editorials.title: Budget built on boom
editorials.body: Government spending is surging on the back of chip-driven tax windfall that may not last The government’s budget proposal for next year, totaling 820.9 trillion won ($599 billion), is the largest ever. The 12.8 percent year-on-year rise and the 92 trillion won increase are also the largest on record. The government’s ability to ramp up spending so substantially is due above all to an exceptional tax revenue windfall brought about by the semiconductor supercycle. The ambitious 162 trillion won Future Response Fund, too, would not have been possible without the surge in corporate tax revenues caused by the semiconductor boom. One cannot help but question how sustainable such a “superexpansionary budget” is. With national debt almost certain to top 1,500 trillion won next year, the government is jacking up spending at an excessive pace. The government budget surpassed 600 trillion won in 2022 and entered the 700 trillion won range this year, four years later. Next year, however, the figure will cross into the 800 trillion won span after just one year. According to government projections, total spending will continue to rise, surpassing 1,000 trillion won in 2030, the final year of President Lee Jae Myung’s term. Many of the programs funded through the Future Response Fund, including support for local areas and young people, as well as education and childcare for infants and young children, are likely to become ongoing programs rather than one-off expenditures. The government has already pledged to expand welfare programs, including providing 1.2 million won a year from birth through age 18 to help young people become self-reliant and offering free education at national universities in the provinces. If tax revenues decline as the semiconductor industry slows, it is questionable whether whichever administration is in power then will be able to cut such spending. If the government inflates the budget on the assumption that a temporary boom will last, it could fall into a vicious cycle of increasing national debt to make up for declining tax revenues. Temporary revenue gains should not be used to justify permanent spending commitments. Thanks to the surge in tax revenues, the government projects that both the managed fiscal deficit and the national debt-to-GDP ratio will decline next year. This amounts to saying that the government can improve its fiscal health even as it spends more money than ever before. Fiscal health should be judged not by how much the government can spend during a boom, but by whether it can afford to sustain that spending after the boom ends. There are also considerable concerns about chronic wasteful spending in the face of this year’s supersized budget. When the budget is increased sharply all at once, it is only natural that each government ministry will be more tempted to expand existing programs or add new ones. Programs with unclear or overlapping effects, cash handout programs and projects driven by constituency demands are perennial targets of scrutiny. There are also growing concerns that lawmakers’ “note budgets” — pork-barrel projects for their constituencies slipped into the budget at the final stage of deliberations — will become even more rampant ahead of the 2028 general election. The Future Response Fund is no exception. It must not degenerate into a giant government slush fund for catering to politicians’ discretionary demands simply by carrying the name “future.” Sunset provisions should be applied to new programs, while existing programs should be subject to performance evaluations to determine whether they should be continued or discontinued. If the government spends this year’s sharp increase in corporate tax revenues on cash handouts and locks in the resulting spending in ways that make it difficult to cut, it could face serious trouble when the semiconductor industry takes a downturn. The National Assembly must rigorously assess the sustainability of spending and carefully scrutinize the merits of each program to prevent a massive waste of the megasized budget. How S. summaryTr: Yong Hye-in, the nominee for minister of gender equality and family, avoided giving a direct answer to demands that she resign from her dual position as a proportional representative.
The presidential office said it would provide an opportunity for her to explain herself at the confirmation hearing, but concerns within the ruling party remain high.
With public persuasion proving difficult, resolving the controversy has become urgent.
editorial.bodyTr: Yong Hye-in, a Basic Income Party lawmaker nominated as gender equality and family minister, avoided giving a direct answer on Tuesday regarding calls for her resignation from her proportional representative seat, saying instead that "I will prepare well for the confirmation hearing." While the presidential office stated the previous day that "there should be an opportunity to make a case through the confirmation process," even within the ruling party there are concerns about her holding dual positions.
